strongestAlternative.why: Alec Pierce projects 10.3 points higher than Harrison (117.8 vs 107.5), sits in the scarcer WR tier 11 (2 left, atRisk=1), and Juancho's raw simulation actually prefers him (dPlan +1.1 vs 0).

advice.strongestCounterargument: Juancho's raw plan value is higher for Alec Pierce (1362.6) and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (1362.7) than for Harrison (1361.5), and Pierce still survives to our next pick 38.3% of the time — so the simulation says the better final roster comes from taking Pierce/JCM and Harrison is only on top because of First Seed's rank anchor.
advice.whyRecommendationStillWins: Those plan differences are 1.1-1.2 points on a 1361-point roster — statistical noise — while the availability spread is not: Harrison survives 6% and Pierce 38.3%, and in the joint runs at least one of them is there 22% of the time meaning the correct sequencing is to take the 6% player now and try for the 38% player at 109. Pierce's projection edge is also standard-scoring volume on a low-target profile, whereas Harrison carries the far higher realistic ceiling as a WR2/flex.
